cohort: 38,449,030 pregnancy-related admissions, including 1,469 in liver transplant recipients, between 2005 and 2013 in the United States
finding: Pregnancy after liver transplant is associated with higher rates of pregnancy complications, including miscarriage, intrauterine growth restriction, postpartum hemorrhage, hypertension, preeclampsia, and thromboembolism, as well as higher rates of caesarean delivery, longer hospital stays, and higher costs, but not an increased risk of mortality.
mod_finding: Liver transplant recipients were more likely to undergo a caesarean delivery (60% vs 36%) compared with the general population.
